done_when: The real-model Codex tests run only when FORGE_LIVE_CODEX=1, which the codex-smoke workflow sets; every other run skips them with a reason naming that variable.

findings.body: When FORGE_LIVE_CODEX is unset or differs from "1" and the SDK is absent, both tests skip with the SDK-installation reason, which does not name FORGE_LIVE_CODEX. Python applies the lower decorator first; pytest [appends markers](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9.1.1/src/_pytest/mark/structures.py#L440-L456) and [returns the first matching skip reason](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9.1.1/src/_pytest/skipping.py#L158-L174). The existing SDK guard at tests/test_codex_smoke.py:128 and tests/test_fix_codex_test_home.py:44 therefore wins. Reverse the decorators in both files so the opt-in reason takes precedence. The supplied close result covers the SDK-installed case only.

findings.body: The supplied repository review rule requires changes to a setting workers can use to update src/forge/templates/skill.md or src/forge/templates/brief.md in the same change. This introduces FORGE_LIVE_CODEX as the required opt-in for running the real-model checks, but neither template is updated. The existing worker brief at src/forge/templates/brief.md:100 discusses handling local real-Codex test failures without explaining the new opt-in. Update a template to explain how workers deliberately run these checks and that ordinary suite runs skip them.
findings.title: Document the live-Codex opt-in in the worker template

why: Two tests call a real Codex model in every local close once the SDK is installed, so closes are slow and fail when the model answers differently
